top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is one identifiable invention (magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the differential light shift for many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime) with a quantitative realization near 10^-18 that has been checked by comparison between independent devices in several laboratories and species. The two-name allocation maps onto concept and first realization (Katori) and record performance plus the many-body fermion clock (Ye), and a citation naming magic-wavelength trapping separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is a strong, productive discovery but its three-name credit leaves out Yuan Cao and early confirming groups and its interpretation is still moving, so it ranks second; no award ranks last because a mature, well-attributed candidate exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my instrumentation work (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO, XL-Calibur) has no documented tie to the optical clock or moire graphene candidates
